name: humanoid-tree-tall-continue

jobs.name: gpu-info
jobs.command: nvidia-smi | tee gpu-info.txt && nvcc --version | tee -a gpu-info.txt

jobs.name: build-humanoid-tall
jobs.command: set -o pipefail; mkdir -p experimental/duck_cuda/build-humanoid-tall; nvcc -std=c++17 -O3 --fmad=false -gencode arch=compute_89,code=sm_89 -gencode arch=compute_120,code=sm_120 -Ihumanoid/variants/h1_tall/include -Iexperimental/duck_cuda/include -Xcompiler -fPIC -shared experimental/duck_cuda/src/duck_cuda.cu -o experimental/duck_cuda/build-humanoid-tall/libhumanoid_cuda.so 2>&1 | tee build-humanoid-tall.log; nvcc -std=c++17 -O3 --fmad=true -gencode arch=compute_89,code=sm_89 -gencode arch=compute_120,code=sm_120 -Ihumanoid/variants/h1_tall/include -Iexperimental/duck_cuda/include -Xcompiler -fPIC -shared experimental/duck_cuda/src/duck_cuda.cu -o experimental/duck_cuda/build-humanoid-tall/libhumanoid_cuda_fast.so 2>&1 | tee -a build-humanoid-tall.log; g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -ffp-contract=off -Ihumanoid/variants/h1_tall/include -Iexperimental/duck_cuda/include -fPIC -shared experimental/duck_cuda/src/duck_cuda_serial.cpp -o experimental/duck_cuda/build-humanoid-tall/libhumanoid_cuda_serial.so 2>&1 | tee -a build-humanoid-tall.log; ls -la experimental/duck_cuda/build-humanoid-tall | tee -a build-humanoid-tall.log

jobs.name: train
jobs.command: set -o pipefail; PY=$(command -v python3); $PY -c 'import numpy' 2>/dev/null || $PY -m pip install --quiet numpy; $PY -B -m walk.train.gpu_train --robot humanoid --variant h1_tall --envs 16384 --horizon 64 --updates 99999 --seed 917 --device cuda --library experimental/duck_cuda/build-humanoid-tall/libhumanoid_cuda_fast.so --lane-env --curriculum humanoid-walk --rsi-fraction 0.5 --policy ff --resume runs/warmstart-tall.pt --accept-every 16 --out gpu-train-out --lr 3e-4 --max-wall-s 600 2>&1 | tee gpu-train.log

accept_probe_note: --accept-every 16: every 16 updates (~2 min at the measured ~7.4 s/update for 16384 envs x 64) the in-run probe judges the current policy on the FROZEN humanoid judge over the CPU harness's exact 12 cells (seeds 4242/7/1913/90210 x 0.50/0.75/1.00 m/s, 8 s) as one E=12 batch on a fresh CUDA-lane instance (DR/gate-termination/RSI off). MEASURED on the RTX 5090 (leg 20260902-155451): 8.4-8.5 s per probe (per-tick D2H readback of 12 envs x 4000 ticks dominates; the serial lane locally takes 3.2 s), so N=8 would have cost ~14 % of a 600 s leg; N=16 -> ~5 probes x 8.5 s ~= 43 s (7 %). AUTHORITY: the fp32 CUDA lane is NOT the judge's lane -- that same leg's on-device 12/12 scored 10/12 on the CPU harness (two 1.0 m/s alternation cells) -- so on cuda the trainer only NOMINATES: two consecutive 12/12 probes write gpu-train-out/accepted/{actor_accepted.pt, candidate_<update>.pt} (listed artifacts, newest 5 kept), print 'HUMANOID WALKING ACCEPTED-CANDIDATE' and training continues to --max-wall-s; gpu/chain.py re-judges every candidate with the CPU harness and stops only on a CPU-confirmed 12/12. Motivation: H1-STOCKY sat at 11/12 for three consecutive legs failing a DIFFERENT single cell each time -- a stochastic tail an end-of-leg judgment cannot catch but an in-run probe can.
